note:
state/triage-repeat/

/.park, one TSV line `\t\t\t\ttriage-repeat-refused: ` (column 6, BH-9863: triage_shard_qsig, the key's build records and its blocker's state; absent on an older 5-column park), and .commented (the board id the comment was posted for): bin/lib/triage-repeat-park.sh, written by bin/triage-shard.sh on a `call-guard repeat` refusal and read by the dispatcher (bin/lib/rt/shards.sh) and bin/lib/stuckqueue-escalate.sh. Deleted when the board entry changes, when the qsig changes (the .park only, .commented stays), and after TRIAGE_REPEAT_PARK_KEEP_S. The fleet-wide record is the D1 ticket_events row from lifecycle_note. Losing it costs at most 1 refused shard at $0 and 1 duplicate comment. Machine-local, never carried

state/stuckqueue-escalate/

/.n, one line ` `: bin/lib/stuckqueue-escalate.sh, called by bin/pipeline-health.sh check 1. Deleted when its queue file is gone (sqe_prune). Losing it costs at most 1 more critical message after 5 more firings. Machine-local, never carried

authority: the per-run fired-alert list of bin/pipeline-health.sh (BH-9818)
note: state/health-fired.<pid> (plus .sorted and .sp siblings), one alert key per line: every alert condition that held this run, written by bin/pipeline-health.sh ($FIRED) and read by its own retraction epilogue, which compares it with state/health-active.txt. Scoped to 1 run by its pid. Losing it costs at most 1 tick of missed retractions. Machine-local, never carried
